sections.h2: What makes the Melissa market different from other Collin County cities?
sections.html:
Melissa is small, young and almost entirely owner-occupied, so most competing listings are recent construction. An older or unrenovated house has to hold its own against builder product with current finishes.

The Census Bureau counted 4,695 residents in 2010 and 13,901 in 2020, then estimated 29,969 on July 1, 2025. That is growth of 115.6 percent over the 2020 base, among the fastest in the state. Children make up 30.7 percent of residents.

  • An agent listing suits a house in good shape with time for showings.
  • A private sale suits an owner comfortable with contracts.
  • A cash purchase suits a house with repairs, tenants or a deadline.

sections.h2: What does the Census say about housing and incomes in Melissa?
sections.html:
Melissa is an owner-heavy, high-income city. The 2020-2024 owner-occupied rate is 88.7 percent, the median home value $454,000 and the median household income $138,763.

The 33.6 minute commute is the longest of the four cities in this group, so many residents drive to jobs elsewhere in the Dallas area. Just 6.7 percent of residents are 65 or older, which marks a young-family market.

Melissa is on U.S. Highway 75 about seven miles northeast of McKinney in north central Collin County. Settlers came in the 1840s for the Blackland Prairie soil, and the town was laid out in 1872 when the Houston and Texas Central Railway arrived.

The Handbook of Texas says a post office opened in May 1873 and an electric interurban line linked the town to Dallas from 1908. A tornado on April 13, 1921 killed thirteen people and a fire later burned many rebuilt buildings. Population slid to 285 by 1949.

Incorporation came in the early 1970s, and the count was 604 in 1980 and 1,350 in 2000. Almost everything people now buy and sell in Melissa went up after that, which is why most houses are only a few years old.

sections.h2: Which Collin County offices matter when selling in Melissa?
sections.html:
Collin County offices handle Melissa houses. The Collin Central Appraisal District sets values and processes exemptions, and the county clerk records the deed.

  • Pull up your account on the district's property search and confirm the homestead exemption is in place.
  • The district's homepage said 2026 notices of appraised value for real property would be mailed April 15.
  • Protests of value go to the Collin appraisal review board.
  • New subdivisions may carry special district charges, so ask the tax office and the title company what appears on your bill.

Ask the county tax office for the balance owed before closing.

sections.h2: How do Texas property tax dates affect a newer Melissa home?
sections.html:
The lien for a year's tax attaches on January 1, which is also the date the appraisal district uses to value the house. Anyone who closes mid-year is dealing with a bill that is already building.

  • School homestead exemption: $140,000, plus $60,000 for owners 65 or older or disabled.
  • A buyer acquiring after January 1 may get the exemption for the rest of that year if the seller did not have it.
  • Notices for homesteads are mailed around April 1, and exemption applications are due before May 1.

Higher values mean tax can be a meaningful line on your closing statement, so have the title company show the proration before you sign.

sections.h2: What if a Melissa house has a tenant?
sections.html:
Rentals are scarce here. The Census Bureau lists a median gross rent of $2,532, and 88.7 percent of homes are owner-occupied, so most buyers want to live in the house themselves.

If a tenant is in place, written notice to vacate is generally three days unless the lease says otherwise. A tenant who stays is sued in justice court and must be served at least four days before trial. Plan your sale date around the lease end.

sections.h2: What if the Melissa owner has died or the loan is in default?
sections.html:
A will can be probated within four years of death, and a muniment of title or affidavit of heirship can be filed with the county clerk. Buyers are not required to accept an affidavit alone. A small estate affidavit works for estates of $75,000 or less not counting the homestead.

On the loan side, the servicer's notice of sale is due at least 21 days before the first-Tuesday auction. Selling first leaves you in charge of price and equity.

faqs.q: Which county is Melissa, TX in?
faqs.a: Collin County, in its north central part near McKinney. The Collin Central Appraisal District and the county clerk handle your values and deed.
Very fast. The Census Bureau counted 13,901 residents in 2020 and estimated 29,969 for July 1, 2025, a 115.6 percent increase over the 2020 base.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Melissa house with a tenant in it?
faqs.a: Yes, though many buyers want to move in. Check the lease end date and give written notice if you need the tenant out.

faqs.q: What homestead exemption can a Melissa owner claim?
faqs.a: School districts must give $140,000, and owners 65 or older or disabled get $60,000 more. File with the appraisal district before May 1.

faqs.q: Do I need probate to sell my late parent's Melissa house?
faqs.a: Usually. Options include probate, a muniment of title or a small estate affidavit. A transfer on death deed recorded before the death skips probate.
